proposed.text: A prestressed concrete floor member requires a 3-hour fire resistance rating. What minimum concrete cover over the prestressing tendons does PD 1096 require?

options.text: 25 millimeters of cover over the prestressing tendons
40 millimeters of cover over the prestressing tendons
50 millimeters of cover over the prestressing tendons
65 millimeters of cover over the prestressing tendons

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 603 specifies prestressed concrete cover requirements: 25mm for 1-hour, 40mm for 2-hour, 50mm for 3-hour, and 65mm for 4-hour ratings. Prestressed tendons require more cover than mild steel because they lose tensile strength at lower temperatures.
proposed.explanation: Prestressing tendons (high-strength steel wire or strand) are more sensitive to elevated temperatures than conventional mild steel reinforcement. They begin losing significant tensile strength at around 300°C, versus 500°C for mild steel. This is why prestressed members require substantially greater cover — 50mm vs. 25mm at the 3-hour level.
